title: Chapter 11. Balarama Dasa, Yadunandana, Kanu Dasa and Others: Praise of Gaura, His Bhavas in Navadvipa, the Sannyasa, Nityananda in Gauda
html:
This chapter completes the core — padas of the Lord's contemporaries known from the Padakalpataru (PK), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) and the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are the remaining padas signed by Balarama Dasa; padas of Yadunandana Chakravarti (a disciple of Gadadhara Dasa) cited by Narahari Chakravarti in the Bhakti-ratnakara; and padas of Kanu Dasa (Kanu Thakura), Raya Ananta, Murari and Krishnadasa, in the order of the lilas: praise of the Gaura-avatara and of Nitai-Chaitanya; Gaura's form and His bhavas in the kirtanas of Navadvipa, when, holding Gadadhara's hand, He speaks of Radha and Vrindavana; the lament over the sannyasa; Shachi in Shantipura; the Lord in Nilachala; Nityananda, sent to Gauda, with Shachi; Gaura's bliss after long separation. Majumdar counts among the Lord's contemporaries Balarama Dasa (on the strength of three BR padas, translated in chapter 10) and Yadunandana (on the strength of his BR padas); the signature "Balarama Dasa" in PK covers padas of several poets, so the attribution of the rest is doubtful. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, BR, the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and KGC; the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Balarama Dasa — "baraṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana…" (PK 2212)

Praise of the Gaura-avatara: making no distinction of varnas and ashramas, of rich and destitute, Gaura gives away the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma; sinners, beasts and birds weep; kings, yogis and jnanis abandon their own — only the poet's heart seems made of stone. Raga suhai.1

বরণ-আশ্রম কিঞ্চন অকিঞ্চন
কার কোন দোষ নাহি মানে ।
শিব-বিরিঞ্চির অগোচর প্রেম-ধন
যাচিয়া বিলায় জগ-জনে ॥

baraṇa-āśrama kiñcana akiñcana
kāra kona doṣa nāhi māne |
śiba-biriñcira agocara prema-dhana
yāciyā bilāya jaga-jane ||

baraṇa-āśrama — varnas and ashramas; kiñcana — those who have; akiñcana — those who have not; kāra — whose; kona doṣa — any fault; nāhi māne — takes no account; śiba-biriñcira — of Shiva and Brahma; agocara — inaccessible; prema-dhana — the treasure of prema; yāciyā — offering of Himself; bilāya — distributes; jaga-jane — to the people of the world

1.1Making no distinction of varnas and ashramas, of those who have and those who have not,
He takes no account of anyone's faults;
the treasure of prema, inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma,
He distributes to the people of the world, offering it Himself.2

করুণার সাগর গৌর-অবতার
নিছনি লইয়া মরি ।
কে জানে কিবা গুণ কিবা সে মাধুরী
প্রাণ কান্দে পাসরিতে নারি ॥

karuṇāra sāgara gaura-abatāra
nichani laiyā mari |
ke jāne kibā guṇa kibā se mādhurī
prāṇa kānde pāsarite nāri ||

karuṇāra sāgara — an ocean of mercy; gaura-abatāra — the incarnation of Gaura; nichani laiyā mari — I would die taking (His) misfortune on myself; ke jāne — who knows; kibā guṇa — what qualities; kibā se mādhurī — what that sweetness; prāṇa kānde — my soul weeps; pāsarite nāri — I cannot forget

1.2An ocean of mercy is the incarnation of Gaura:
I would give my life to turn misfortune away from Him!3
Who knows what His qualities are, what His sweetness is?
My soul weeps — I cannot forget.

পামর পাষণ্ড আদি দীন হীন খীণ জাতি
গুণ শুনি কান্দে জগ-জন ।
অগেয়ান পশু পাখী তারা কান্দে ঝরে আঁখি
কি দিয়া বান্ধিল সভার মন ॥

pāmara pāṣaṇḍa ādi dīna hīna khīṇa jāti
guṇa śuni kānde jaga-jana |
ageyāna paśu pākhī tārā kānde jhare ām̐khi
ki diyā bāndhila sabhāra mana ||

pāmara — the low; pāṣaṇḍa — the godless; ādi — and the rest; dīna — the poor; hīna — the wretched; khīṇa jāti — the weak and low-born; guṇa śuni — hearing of the qualities; kānde — weeps; jaga-jana — the whole world; ageyāna — unreasoning; paśu pākhī — beasts and birds; tārā kānde — they too weep; jhare ām̐khi — (tears) pour from the eyes; ki diyā — with what; bāndhila — has bound; sabhāra mana — the hearts of all

1.3The low, the godless, the poor, the wretched, the weak and the low-born —
hearing of His qualities, the whole world weeps;
even unreasoning beasts and birds weep, tears pour from their eyes:
with what has He bound the hearts of all?4

রাজা ছাড়ে রাজা-ভোগ যোগী ছাড়ে ধ্যান যোগ
জ্ঞানী কান্দে ছাড়ি জ্ঞান-রস ।
কেবা বলরাম-হিয়া গঢ়িল পাষাণ দিয়া
হেন রস না কৈল পরশ ॥

rājā chāṛe rājā-bhoga yogī chāṛe dhyāna yoga
jñānī kānde chāṛi jñāna-rasa |
kebā balarāma-hiyā gaṛhila pāṣāṇa diyā
hena rasa nā kaila paraśa ||

rājā chāṛe — the king abandons; rājā-bhoga — royal pleasures; yogī chāṛe — the yogi abandons; dhyāna yoga — meditation and yoga; jñānī kānde — the jnani weeps; chāṛi — abandoning; jñāna-rasa — the taste of knowledge; kebā — who; balarāma-hiyā — Balarama's heart; gaṛhila — fashioned; pāṣāṇa diyā — out of stone; hena rasa — this rasa; nā kaila paraśa — did not touch

1.4The king abandons royal pleasures, the yogi meditation and yoga,
the jnani weeps, abandoning the taste of knowledge.
Who, then, fashioned Balarama's heart out of stone,
that this rasa has not touched it?

2. Balarama Dasa — "dekha dekha aparūpa gaura-carita…" (PK 2286)

Gaura's pastimes are like those of Vamana: the Lord of Gokula has appeared again, and Prataparudra, like Bali, gave Him body, mind and all his possessions, asuras such as Jagai and Madhai bowed to His feet; Advaita is Bhagiratha, who brought down the Ganga of bhakti, Nityananda is Shiva, who received it; in it all the devotees bathe, and the fallen attain the supreme abode. Raga kamoda.5

দেখ দেখ অপরূপ গৌর-চরিত ।
সো গোকুল-পতি অব পরকাশল
পুন কিয়ে বামন-রীত ॥ ধ্রু ॥

dekha dekha aparūpa gaura-carita |
so gokula-pati aba parakāśala
puna kiye bāmana-rīta || dhru ||

dekha dekha — look, look; aparūpa — wondrous; gaura-carita — Gaura's deeds; so gokula-pati — that Lord of Gokula; aba parakāśala — has now appeared; puna kiye — is it not again; bāmana-rīta — the manner of Vamana

2.1(Refrain) Look, look — wondrous are Gaura's deeds!
That very Lord of Gokula has now appeared —
was it not so that Vamana once appeared?6

নিরখি প্রতাপ প্রতাপরুদ্র বলি
তনু মন সরবস দেল ।
জগাই মাধাই আদি অসুরগণ
চরণ প্রবণ নিজ কেল ॥

nirakhi pratāpa pratāparudra bali
tanu mana sarabasa dela |
jagāi mādhāi ādi asuragaṇa
caraṇa prabaṇa nija kela ||

nirakhi — seeing; pratāpa — the majesty; pratāparudra — Prataparudra; bali — (like) Bali; tanu mana — body and mind; sarabasa — all possessions; dela — gave; jagāi mādhāi ādi — Jagai, Madhai and the rest; asura-gaṇa — the asuras; caraṇa prabaṇa — bowed to the feet; nija kela — made His own

2.2Seeing His majesty, Prataparudra, like Bali,
gave Him body, mind and all he possessed;
Jagai, Madhai and the other asuras
He brought to bow at His feet.7

যছু পদ সহ অদ্বৈত-ভগীরথ
ভকতি-গঙ্গ-পরবাহ ।
নিত্যানন্দ গিরিশ দেই আনল
বাম-হিমাচল মাহ ॥

yachu pada saha advaita-bhagīratha
bhakati-gaṅga-parabāha |
nityānanda giriśa dei ānala
bāma-himācala māha ||

yachu pada — from whose feet; saha — together with; advaita-bhagīratha — Advaita as Bhagiratha; bhakati-gaṅga-parabāha — the stream of the Ganga of bhakti; nityānanda giriśa — Nityananda is Girisha (Shiva); dei — receiving (it); ānala — brought (down); bāma-himācala māha — into the … Himalaya (the sense of "bāma" is unclear)

2.3From His feet, with Advaita as Bhagiratha,
flowed the stream of the Ganga of bhakti;
Nityananda is Girisha: He received it
and brought it down into the Himalaya…8

যছু অবগাহনে অখিল ভকতগণে
বিলসই প্রেম-আনন্দ ।
পামর পতিত পরম পদ পায়ল
বঞ্চিত বলরাম মন্দ ॥

yachu abagāhane akhila bhakatagaṇe
bilasai prema-ānanda |
pāmara patita parama pada pāyala
bañcita balarāma manda ||

yachu abagāhane — bathing in it; akhila bhakata-gaṇe — all the devotees; bilasai — revel; prema-ānanda — in the bliss of prema; pāmara patita — the low and fallen; parama pada — the supreme abode; pāyala — attained; bañcita — left out; balarāma manda — worthless Balarama

2.4Bathing in it, all the devotees
revel in the bliss of prema;
the low and the fallen attained the supreme abode —
only worthless Balarama is left out.9

3. Raya Ananta — "nitāi caitanya duṭī bhāi dayāra abadhi…" (KGC 28.2)

Nitai and Chaitanya, two brothers, are the limit of mercy: the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma and sought in vain by the four Vedas They give away unceasingly; the fallen of the age of Kali, crying "Nitai-Chaitanya", dance and sing. Raga shri.10

নিতাই চৈতন্য দুটী ভাই দয়ার অবধি ।
শিব ব্রহ্মার দুর্লভ প্রেম যাচে নিরবধি ॥

nitāi caitanya duṭī bhāi dayāra abadhi |
śiba brahmāra durlabha prema yāce nirabadhi ||

nitāi caitanya — Nitai and Chaitanya; duṭī bhāi — two brothers; dayāra abadhi — the limit of mercy; śiba brahmāra — of Shiva and Brahma; durlabha prema — the inaccessible prema; yāce — give away (offering it); nirabadhi — without end

3.1Nitai and Chaitanya, two brothers, are the limit of mercy:
the prema inaccessible to Shiva and Brahma They give away without end.

চারি বেদে অন্বেষয়ে যে প্রেম পাইতে ।
হেন প্রেম দুটী ভাই যাচে অবিরতে ॥

cāri bede anveṣaye ye prema pāite |
hena prema duṭī bhāi yāce abirate ||

cāri bede — the four Vedas; anveṣaye — search; ye prema — the prema which; pāite — to attain; hena prema — such prema; duṭī bhāi — the two brothers; yāce — give away; abirate — unceasingly

3.2The prema which the four Vedas search for, to attain it —
such prema the two brothers give away unceasingly.

পতিত দুর্গত যত কলি-হত যারা ।
নিতাই চৈতন্য বলি নাচে গায় তারা ॥

patita durgata yata kali-hata yārā |
nitāi caitanya bali nāce gāya tārā ||

patita — the fallen; durgata — the wretched; yata — as many as; kali-hata — struck down by Kali; yārā — those who; nitāi caitanya bali — crying "Nitai-Chaitanya"; nāce gāya — dance and sing; tārā — they

3.3The fallen, the wretched, as many as are struck down by Kali —
crying "Nitai-Chaitanya!" they dance and sing.11

ভুবন-মঙ্গল ভেল সঙ্কীর্তন-রসে ।
রায় অনন্ত কাঁদে না পাইয়া শেষে ॥

bhubana-maṅgala bhela saṅkīrtana-rase |
rāya ananta kām̐de nā pāiyā śeṣe ||

bhubana-maṅgala — the good of the world; bhela — has come about; saṅkīrtana-rase — in the rasa of sankirtana; rāya ananta — Raya Ananta; kām̐de — weeps; nā pāiyā — not obtaining; śeṣe — at the last (GPT1 "leśe" — not a particle)

3.4The good of the whole world has come about in the rasa of sankirtana —
Raya Ananta weeps: not a drop of it has come to him.12

4. Krishnadasa — "soṅaro naba gauracanda…" (PK 1085)

Remembering the youthful Gaurachandra — the moon of Navadvipa, Krishna Himself: the moon-face, eyes full of prema, locks dressed with flowers, earrings, the Kaustubha, red garments, sandal; the king of serpents holds an umbrella over Him, Lakshmi serves His feet, the devotees sing His glory; at the end the poet places his hope in Nitai too, the giver of prema. Raga bhairavi.13

সোঙরো নব গৌরচন্দ
নাগর বনয়ারি ।
নবদ্বীপ-ইন্দু করুণা-সিন্ধু
ভক্ত-বৎসলকারী ॥ ধ্রু ॥

soṅaro naba gauracanda
nāgara banayāri |
nabadvīpa-indu karuṇā-sindhu
bhakta-batsalakārī || dhru ||

soṅaro — I remember; naba — the youthful; gauracanda — Gaurachandra; nāgara — the graceful (youth); banayāri — Vanamali (Krishna); nabadvīpa-indu — the moon of Navadvipa; karuṇā-sindhu — the ocean of mercy; bhakta-batsala-kārī — tenderly loving the devotees

4.1(Refrain) I remember the youthful Gaurachandra —
the graceful Vanamali,
the moon of Navadvipa, the ocean of mercy,
tenderly loving His devotees.14

বদন-চন্দ অধর রঙ্গ
নয়নে গলত প্রেম-তরঙ্গ
চন্দ্র কোটি ভানু কোটি
শোভা নিছয়ারি ।
কুসুম-শোভিত চাঁচর চিকুর
ললাটে তিলক নাসিকা উজোর
দশন মোতিম অমিয়া হাস
দামিনি ঘনয়ারি ॥

badana-canda adhara raṅga
nayane galata prema-taraṅga
candra koṭi bhānu koṭi
śobhā nichayāri |
kusuma-śobhita cām̐cara cikura
lalāṭe tilaka nāsikā ujora
daśana motima amiyā hāsa
dāmini ghanayāri ||

badana-canda — the moon-face; adhara raṅga — red lips; nayane — from the eyes; galata — stream; prema-taraṅga — waves of prema; candra koṭi — millions of moons; bhānu koṭi — millions of suns; śobhā — the beauty; nichayāri — I offer as a gift to ward off harm; kusuma-śobhita — dressed with flowers; cām̐cara cikura — the curling locks; lalāṭe tilaka — tilaka on the brow; nāsikā ujora — the shining nose; daśana motima — teeth are pearls; amiyā hāsa — the smile is nectar; dāmini — lightning; ghanayāri — (in) a cloud

4.2His face is the moon, His lips are red,
waves of prema stream from His eyes;
the beauty of millions of moons, of millions of suns
I offer to Him as a gift to ward off harm.
His locks, dressed with flowers,
the tilaka on His brow, His shining nose,
His teeth are pearls, His smile nectar,
like lightning in a cloud.15

মকর-কুণ্ডল ঝলকে গণ্ড
মণি-কৌস্তুভ-দীপ্ত কণ্ঠ
অরুণ বসন করুণ বচন
শোভা অতি ভারি ।
মাল্য-চন্দন-চর্চিত অঙ্গ
লাজে লজ্জিত কোটি অনঙ্গ
অঙ্গদ বলয়া রতন-নূপুর
যজ্ঞ-সূত্রধারি ॥

makara-kuṇḍala jhalake gaṇḍa
maṇi-kaustubha-dīpta kaṇṭha
aruṇa basana karuṇa bacana
śobhā ati bhāri |
mālya-candana-carcita aṅga
lāje lajjita koṭi anaṅga
aṅgada balayā ratana-nūpura
yajña-sūtradhāri ||

makara-kuṇḍala — makara earrings; jhalake — flash; gaṇḍa — (on) the cheeks; maṇi-kaustubha-dīpta — lit by the Kaustubha gem; kaṇṭha — the neck; aruṇa basana — red garments; karuṇa bacana — merciful words; śobhā ati bhāri — beauty beyond measure; mālya-candana-carcita — anointed with sandal and garlanded; aṅga — the body; lāje lajjita — put to shame; koṭi anaṅga — millions of Kamadevas; aṅgada — armlets; balayā — bracelets; ratana-nūpura — jewelled anklets; yajña-sūtra-dhāri — wearing the sacred thread

4.3Makara earrings flash on His cheeks,
His neck is lit by the Kaustubha gem,
red garments, merciful words —
beauty beyond measure.
His body anointed with sandal, in garlands —
millions of Kamadevas are put to shame;
bracelets on arms and wrists, jewelled anklets,
the sacred thread upon Him.16

ছত্র ধরত ধরণিধরেন্দ্র
গাওত যশ ভকতবৃন্দ
কমলা-সেবিত পাদদ্বন্দ্ব
বলিয়ে বলিহারি ।
কহত দান কৃষ্ণদাস
গৌর-চরণে করত আশ
পতিত-পাবন নিতাই চান্দ
প্রেম দানকারী ॥

chatra dharata dharaṇidharendra
gāota yaśa bhakatabṛnda
kamalā-sebita pādadvandva
baliye balihāri |
kahata dāna kṛṣṇadāsa
gaura-caraṇe karata āśa
